MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This is essentially a negative-only neuron: its meaningful (large-magnitude) responses are strong suppressions on the highly predictable continuation token inside a fixed multiword expression, idiom, or proper name (e.g. "fall-off**-the**-bone", "six **Pro** Bowls", "Schools **of** Business", "loved ones **remaining** behind"), while its "top" positive activations are tiny, diffuse, and mostly on similarly formulaic filler tokens ("as **soon** as", "Join LinkedIn **today**", "P **Street** NW").

L31·N2305unmasked layer
This neuron has no single lexical trigger — it fires diffusely on ordinary mid-clause tokens (function words like " is", " for", "…", or nouns like " difficulties", " reader") inside formal, impersonal expository/academic-journalistic prose, and is strongly suppressed on comparable tokens in informal first-person/conversational or forum-style writing (" memo", " wealth", " a", " it"), so it appears to encode a formal-expository register signal rather than a specific word.

L31·N9187unmasked layer
This neuron has no single lexical trigger; it peaks on the word that completes a strongly context-constrained collocation or set phrase (e.g. "are **held** at", "on the **frontline**", "represent Pakistan **at** the UN", "the original **order** of", "runs from **5** pm"), i.e. a highly predictable continuation slot, and is suppressed on pronouns/auxiliaries and clause-final punctuation in loose conversational text.

L31·N12222unmasked layer
This neuron fires on a single mid-sentence word (usually a function word or head noun/verb) that opens a highly predictable collocation/continuation — e.g. "is **often** necessary", "**for** easy and discreet", "people **would** not consider", "a **voucher** holder", "characters **who** work together", "can **offer** protection" — rather than on any consistent semantic category; it is strongly suppressed by sentence/clause-initial adverbs and list commas ("Successfully", "since", "technologies**,** culture and…").

L31·N13814unmasked layer
This neuron fires on mid-phrase function words and sub-word pieces sitting inside highly formulaic/predictable collocations — the "the" of "to the top", the "a" of "fitting of a five-star hotel", "across" in "came across", the "=" in a URL query string, the letter fragments of abbreviations like "BFA"/"F.B." — i.e. a position just before a near-deterministic continuation, while it is strongly suppressed on the token that *completes* such a fixed expression ("face value", "WBS", "we can provide").
